title: Verified-Guardian Credential Built on Childcare Centers
one_liner: Start as a custody-aware pickup and consent app for childcare centers, then turn those institutions into issuers of privacy-preserving 'verified parent of a child aged X' tokens that apps pay for.
customer: First: childcare centers, camps and youth orgs (SaaS at $50-150 per site per month). Later: app stores, game studios and platforms (per-attestation fees), and state agencies.
problem: Parental-consent laws (Ohio, Florida, Texas and others) need a verified parent, but credit-card or ID checks prove adulthood, not parenthood. OS vendors will supply age attestation but not guardian relationships. Meanwhile childcare centers and schools already verify guardian-child relationships, custody orders and authorized pickup, and that verification is not reusable.
solution: Phase 1 is a check-in and pickup app with ID and liveness verification for guardians, custody-order parsing, an authorized pickup list, and e-consent for photos, trips and immunizations. Phase 2 lets the center vouch, through zero-knowledge or selective-disclosure tokens, that an adult is a verified guardian of a child in an age band, without revealing identities to apps.
why_now: Consent laws took effect in mid-2026, OS-level age signals exist (California, Texas), and age-verification breaches have made 'verify once, store nothing' attractive. Zero-knowledge age-proof libraries appeared in 2025 (from memory), and the brief identifies guardian and consent workflows as the gap OS vendors won't fill.
revenue_model: Center SaaS ($50-150 per site per month) now, and per-attestation fees ($0.10-0.50) from platforms later, with revenue share to issuing centers.
non_obvious_insight: Identity startups verify people, but the missing primitive is verifying a relationship. The institutions that already do it (childcare centers with custody paperwork) form an unmonetized, fragmented long tail.
first_30_days: Interview 20 center directors about pickup disputes and custody paperwork. Build an MVP with QR pickup and a custody-document vault. Sell 10 centers at $79 a month. Integrate an ID-verification vendor for guardian checks and sketch the token format with a privacy engineer.

title: Benefits Administrator for Pet-Care Subsidies
one_liner: When hundreds of millions in philanthropy and city funds must reach the right households through thousands of small clinics, someone needs the HSA-administrator equivalent: eligibility, vouchers, payment and audit.
customer: Foundation grantees and programs (Duffield and PetSmart Charities recipients), county animal services and spay-neuter voucher programs. Clinics are the redemption side.
problem: Duffield committed $250M over 5 years, starting with 250 grants of $10K plus $10M in multi-year awards. Grantees run eligibility by paper forms and spreadsheets, clinics wait weeks for reimbursement, funders cannot compare cost per pet outcome, and fraud and overhead eat funds.
solution: Verify proxy eligibility (SNAP, Medicaid, housing-voucher documents or benefit APIs), issue capped QR or card vouchers by procedure category, pay clinics within 5 business days, and export standardized reporting (pets treated, cost, outcome, declined) to funders. Define a shared outcome taxonomy that becomes the field standard.
why_now: The $250M Duffield commitment (2026-09-17) and PetSmart Charities' $100M created hundreds of new grantees at once. Card-issuing and instant-payout APIs let a small team run a closed-loop voucher program.
revenue_model: 4-7% administration fee on disbursed dollars (funded from grant overhead lines), SaaS fee per grantee, and data and reporting subscriptions for funders.
non_obvious_insight: Money is not the binding constraint; distribution rails are. Human benefit administrators (HSA and EBT processors) became large businesses because funders needed accountability. About 250 first-round grantees have no back office, so the standard-setter for outcomes measurement owns the funders' reporting.
first_30_days: Contact 20 first-round grantees and 5 county animal services. Offer a free voucher tool to one program with a $10K grant, run through 3 clinics, and publish an outcomes one-pager. Then brief funder program officers on standardized reporting.

title: Payroll and Proof-of-Trust for Household Staff
one_liner: A WhatsApp payroll, advance and verified-record product for Nigeria's drivers, housekeepers, nannies and gatemen, paid for by their employers.
customer: Middle- and upper-income households in Lagos and Abuja (Lekki, Ikoyi, VI, Ikeja GRA, Maitama) that employ domestic staff. Placement agencies as a channel. Diaspora children who pay for home-care of ageing parents.
problem: Millions of household workers are paid in cash or ad-hoc transfers, with no records, no pension, no health cover and no credit history. Employers act as lender of last resort, giving 3-5 untracked advances a year for school fees and emergencies. That breeds resentment, sudden resignations and theft accusations. Placement agencies charge roughly a month's salary and rely on 'guarantor forms' that everyone knows can be faked. Staff are excluded from credit even after 10 years of steady pay.
solution: The employer sets each worker's salary and pay date on WhatsApp and pays through the platform. The system runs an NIN/BVN check at hire, records every advance and auto-deducts repayment from next month's pay, and keeps a payslip history. The worker gets a wallet, an optional micro-pension contribution and health-cover add-on, and a payment-history record that lenders can use for the first genuine loan of their life. Agencies get a 'verified staff' badge and a share of revenue in return for onboarding their clients.
why_now: Wallet and bank-account penetration among lower-income workers is now high enough that most domestic staff already hold OPay, Moniepoint or PalmPay accounts. NIN/BVN verification APIs are cheap. Salary advances and lending are moving into the regulated FCCPC and CBN perimeter, and households are more cost-squeezed and more digital than in 2020. Voice-note and WhatsApp interfaces in English, Pidgin and Yoruba are finally reliable.
revenue_model: Employer subscription of about N2,000-3,000 per worker per month. A small fee on advances routed through employer-funded 'advance limits'. Commissions on micro-pension, health-cover and eventual worker microloans. Placement-agency referral share and verified-staff certificate fees.
non_obvious_insight: The real customer is the employer's peace of mind, not the worker's financial inclusion. Households will pay to stop the awkward informal-lender relationship and the fear of being scammed by staff with fake guarantors. The worker's payment history is a credit dataset that no bureau holds, and the employer pays to create it.
first_30_days: Ship a WhatsApp bot with a simple payslip and advance ledger, using a bank-partner payout API. Sign 8-10 placement agencies in Lekki, Ikoyi and Maitama and pilot with 100 households through their client lists and estate WhatsApp groups. Charge from day one, since these households are not price-sensitive. Use the first 300 workers' history to design a pilot micro-loan with a partner MFB.

title: Settlement Claim Autopilot for Ticket Buyers
one_liner: A privacy-first app that reconstructs a fan's ticket purchase history and files claims in ticketing settlements and refund orders, paid per validated claim by administrators and plaintiff firms.
customer: Settlement administrators and plaintiff firms, who pay per validated claim because they are judged on claim rates. Consumers use it free or pay a success fee.
problem: The FTC alleges $3.7B in resale fees from 2019-2024. Live Nation was found liable on monopolization in April 2026. In June 2026 the UK CMA ordered StubHub to refund 50,000+ customers, and World Cup ticket failures triggered class actions in New York and British Columbia. Claim rates in consumer settlements are typically low because buyers cannot reconstruct old purchases.
solution: Fans forward receipt emails or upload data exports (avoiding restricted Gmail scopes at launch). Local parsing rebuilds each purchase (event, price, fee, date) and matches it to open claim windows and prefilled forms. Sell it to administrators as a claims-acquisition channel, and keep watching for new live-events settlements.
why_now: A wave of ticketing liabilities is landing at once, and cheap models can parse messy receipts. Individual recoveries of about $30 are uneconomical for lawyers but work in batch.
revenue_model: $3-15 per validated claim from administrators and law firms, optional 10-15% consumer success fee, and later expansion to other settlement categories.
non_obvious_insight: The real buyer is the administrator or counsel measured on claim rate, not the consumer. Email receipts are better proof than memory, and automation turns tiny per-person recoveries into a scalable business.
first_30_days: Launch a landing page around the CMA StubHub refund order. Pitch 5 administrators and pilot one active claim. Test the receipt-forward parser with 500 users and negotiate a per-claim bounty.

title: Micropollutant Bill Calculator for Generic Drug Makers
one_liner: A dataset and model that estimates each pharma and cosmetics company's share of Europe's new micropollutant treatment bill, sold first to generic manufacturers who cannot pass the cost on.
customer: Generic and OTC drug manufacturers and their trade body, cosmetics makers, and the national producer-responsibility bodies being created to run the scheme. Companies pay subscriptions, and the bodies pay for the allocation licence.
problem: Step one: the revised Urban Wastewater Directive makes pharma and cosmetics makers pay at least 80% of quaternary treatment, with the payment scheme due by end-2028. Cost estimates differ by roughly 10x (EC 1.2B euros, JRC 1.56B, EurEau 3.6-11.2B, Spain alone 24.5B). Step two: each state must allocate cost by load. Step three: generics makers work on thin margins under tender pricing and cannot pass costs through, so they will drop low-margin molecules, causing shortages. Nobody owns the allocation dataset.
solution: A compound-level model of the top 100 active ingredients and cosmetic ingredients: sales volumes from national statistics, excretion and removal rates, ecotoxicity thresholds and plant-upgrade timelines (20% of large plants by 2033, 60% by 2039, 100% by 2045). Output: estimated cost share per marketing-authorisation holder, by state and year, with scenario bands. Compare allocation keys (by mass versus toxicity-weighted).
why_now: Member states are drafting schemes in 2026-2028, and industry lobbying starts now. The 10x cost disagreement means the first credible number will anchor the negotiation.
revenue_model: $30-120k/yr subscriptions per company, $10-20k workshops, and licences to scheme administrators.
non_obvious_insight: The fight is not over whether pharma pays but over how the allocation key is defined, and generics makers and originators want opposite keys. Owning the neutral dataset means owning the terms of the negotiation.
first_30_days: Publish a free 'top 30 molecules' liability preview using public consumption and removal data. Email regulatory-affairs heads at 20 generics makers in Spain, Italy, Poland and India, and at the generics trade body. Sell the first paid workshop for 10-20k euros.

title: Fractional Operator for Tiny Private Water Systems
angle: Pairing 1: SMB back office x Water (lens: compliance and succession x PFAS)
one_liner: A flat-fee compliance back office and operator-of-record for the mobile-home parks, small subdivisions and rural employers that own small water systems and are about to face PFAS testing in 2027.
customer: Owners of mobile-home parks, small private water companies and HOA systems, and rural employers or private schools with their own wells. These are community and non-transient non-community systems, typically under 3,300 people. The owner is often an aging individual or family LLC with no operations staff.
problem: Owners face initial PFAS monitoring in 2027 and a 4.0 ppt limit still on the books. EPA's May 2026 proposal would move compliance from 2029 to 2031 and drop limits on four other compounds. The lead action level tightens on Nov 1, 2027. The whiplash freezes capex. Nobody at the business knows the sampling calendar, the accredited lab, the state portal, or the money ($1B of IIJA earmarked for PFAS testing and treatment, $7.2B of FY2026 SRF). The owner also cannot sell, because a first sample becomes a disclosure.
solution: Wedge: a $1,500 flat 'PFAS-2027 Readiness Pack' covering the sampling plan, lab coordination, result interpretation against 4.0 ppt, state filing and an options memo (treat, interconnect, drill, or sell). Upsell to a $600/mo retainer for the sampling calendar, consumer confidence report, lead inventory, monthly operator logs, tenant submetered billing and bookkeeping for a segregated water fund. The operator-of-record role is subcontracted to a state-certified operator partner. Later, broker and operate systems whose owners want out.
why_now: EPA's May 2026 proposals to delay PFAS compliance and rescind four limits have left small owners paralyzed, while 2027 initial monitoring still stands. Public money is earmarked: $1B IIJA for PFAS, $7.2B FY2026 SRF, and states are pushing consolidation of non-viable systems. The Boomer ownership wave is hitting the same long tail of tiny systems. EPA's science office was eliminated in 2026, so owners get less federal guidance.
revenue_model: $1,500 Readiness Pack. $400-$900/mo retainer per system by size. 6% success fee on SRF or state grants won. 2-4% brokerage fee on systems sold, plus an option to acquire orphan systems at distressed multiples using consolidation money.
non_obvious_insight: Federal delay does not remove the liability that appears at the first sample. Once a 2027 result exists it becomes a disclosure item in any sale, loan or insurance renewal. So the smart small owner samples early and under a plan. The firm that holds the compliance record becomes the natural buyer of last resort for a long tail of systems too small for the big acquirers. The retainer is the cheapest way to source those succession deals.
first_30_days: Sign one retired state-certified operator as partner and one accredited PFAS lab for a bulk rate. Join two state manufactured-housing associations and the state rural water association. Run free 'is my system covered?' webinars. Sell 10 Readiness Packs at $1,500 in one state, and use the results to prep 3 grant applications. Start compliance-only and add operator-of-record after the partner clears state rules.

title: Independent Conformance Bench for CMS-0057-F APIs
one_liner: A testing-and-attestation service that runs the open-source Inferno and Da Vinci test kits against a health plan's real FHIR APIs and produces the evidence pack its compliance officer needs before January 2027.
customer: Small and mid-size Medicaid managed-care plans, regional Medicare Advantage plans, CHIP managed-care entities, TPAs and the small payer-IT vendors serving them. Buyer is the compliance officer or CIO who signed a vendor contract and can't verify it.
problem: CMS-0057-F requires four FHIR APIs (Patient Access, Provider Access, Payer-to-Payer, Prior Authorization) by 1 Jan 2027, and the 72-hour and 7-day decision timelines have applied since Jan 2026. Plans bought vendor stacks and hear 'we're compliant,' but the plan carries the liability. CMS points at ONC's Inferno tooling, yet almost no one independent runs it against the plan's production-like environment and writes the attestation.
solution: A managed test bench: Inferno with the Da Vinci PAS/CRD/DTR and CARIN test kits, Synthea synthetic members mapped to the plan's data model, latency and load tests aligned to the decision-time metrics, and SMART/OAuth security checks. Deliverables are a pass/fail matrix, remediation tickets for the vendor, an executive attestation binder, and quarterly regression runs as vendors ship updates.
why_now: Guidance is that plans commit to a stack by Q3 2026 to leave time for testing, so Q4 2026 is the test window. It is late September. The rule is fixed, the open-source test kits exist, and the buyers' vendors have a conflict of interest in grading themselves.
revenue_model: Fixed-fee readiness assessment of USD 15-40k. Quarterly regression subscription of USD 3-8k per month. Vendor-side 'independently tested' certification fee. Optional remediation project work.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer isn't engineering; it's a compliance officer who needs independent evidence to hold a vendor to account. Inferno has huge adoption among developers but has never been packaged as an auditor's deliverable. Independence, not tooling, is the product.
first_30_days: Spin up a hosted Inferno plus Synthea environment. Publish a free 'CMS-0057-F self-test cheat sheet.' Approach 10 Medicaid MCO compliance officers through state Medicaid association events and LinkedIn. Sell three pilot assessments at about USD 10k to build case studies before year-end. Partner with FHIR consultancies that lack independent status.

title: Continuity Retainer for One-Licensee Funeral Homes
one_liner: Key-person insurance for funeral homes: a bench of pre-credentialed licensed directors and embalmers who step in within 24-48 hours when the owner is sick, burned out or gone, with a built-in path to succession.
customer: Independent and rural funeral homes with one or two licensed staff (roughly 30-150 calls a year), typically owner-operators aged 55-75. A second buyer is the family of an owner who has died or fallen ill and needs the home kept legal while it is sold.
problem: States require a licensed funeral director or manager-in-charge, and often a licensed embalmer, for an establishment to operate. The owner is on call 24/7/365 and hasn't had a real week off in years. One heart attack, surgery or burnout means the home cannot legally operate, families get funneled to the consolidator down the road, and a business built over three generations is sold at a distressed price. Informal 'relief director' phone lists exist, but there is no bench, no contract, no reciprocity or board paperwork handled, and no guarantee anyone answers at 3 a.m.
solution: Recruit retired and semi-retired licensed directors and embalmers, including many leaving consolidators, and pre-credential them in a target state cluster with background checks and reciprocity filings. Sell continuity retainers that guarantee a set number of coverage days a year (real vacations, weekends off) plus emergency activation within 24-48 hours at a day rate. The company handles the state-board notice of interim manager changes. A succession track lets an interim operator or next-generation licensed buyer convert into a partner or buyer with seller financing, so owners have an alternative to a roll-up.
why_now: Consolidation keeps shrinking the independent pool (SCI alone bought about 22 funeral homes and 2 cemeteries for roughly $101M in 2025). The licensed workforce is aging while mortuary-school pipelines are thin. Rising cremation lowers revenue per case, making full-time second hires unaffordable for small homes. Rural closures are creating 'funeral deserts'. Many states have passed occupational-license recognition laws that make multi-state relief staffing easier.
revenue_model: Retainer of $900-$2,000/month per home including N coverage days. Activation day rate of $800-$1,400 billed to the home, with a 25-30% margin over what the licensee is paid. Per-case fees for trade embalming and prep-room services. A 1-2% success fee on succession transactions.
non_obvious_insight: The real asset of an independent funeral home isn't the building, it's one license holder with a phone, and that is a single point of failure. Consolidators know it and wait. Owners will pay to sleep: this is a wellness and continuity product disguised as staffing, and its best feature is the succession pipeline it creates once a trusted operator is already inside the home.
first_30_days: Recruit eight retired licensed directors and embalmers through state association chapters and retiree groups. Check each state board's rules for temporary manager-in-charge designation. Pitch 20 one-licensee homes in two adjacent counties at a $1,200/month founding rate with a 'test weekend off' guarantee. Sign the first three, and run the first covered weekend within 30 days to produce a testimonial.

title: AI-Guided Feline Heart Screening by Technicians
one_liner: Handheld ultrasound with AI probe guidance lets technicians capture heart clips on cats, with remote cardiologist over-read making HCM screening a routine add-on instead of a referral.
customer: General-practice clinics (senior and pre-anesthetic cats), breeders of at-risk breeds, and shelters; later insurers.
problem: Feline hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is common and often silent until clot or heart failure. Screening needs a cardiologist's echo, which is scarce and costs a few hundred dollars, so most cats are never screened. Cat households are growing (53M) and the vet workforce is not.
solution: Existing vet-priced handheld probes, a guidance app that prompts standard views and rejects poor clips (trained on cardiologist-labeled data), and a board-certified over-read within 24 hours with next-step recommendations. Sold as a 'senior cat heart check' and a breeder program.
why_now: AI acquisition guidance for novices has been proven in human echo, handheld ultrasound is cheap, vision models are strong, and remote reading is a way to stretch scarce cardiologists while techs take on more scope.
revenue_model: $60-90 per over-read, probe leasing at about $199 per month, and breeder program fees.
non_obvious_insight: The product is not AI diagnosis; it is AI acquisition guidance so a technician can collect usable images. The scarce resource is the cardiologist's time, so pooling over-reads creates the leverage, and the resulting longitudinal dataset improves guidance and screening protocols.
first_30_days: Sign 1-2 board-certified cardiologists on a per-read basis. Equip 5 clinics with handheld probes and run 100 screening scans. Measure the share of diagnostic-quality clips, then sell a $99 senior cat heart check.

title: Continuity Vault for Solo Operators
one_liner: A break-glass vault, dead-man switch and runbook so a solo business survives its owner's hospitalization or death, and its AI agents stop cleanly.
customer: Solo and two-person business owners aged 45+, reached through independent life-insurance agents, estate attorneys, SBA lenders and CPAs.
problem: For the majority of small businesses that are solo operations, the owner is the only person with access to the bank, domain, Google listing, payroll, customer list and payment processor. When the owner is incapacitated, nobody can legally or technically act. Delegated AI agents and OAuth tokens add new failure modes because they keep acting, or fail, without supervision.
solution: An encrypted vault with a named successor, dead-man switch, and pre-authorized runbook: the top ten bills, customer notification templates, who to call, how to pause automated agents and revoke tokens, and a wind-down-or-sell pack with a handoff to a route or book sale.
why_now: Owners increasingly hand credentials to AI agents and automations, and the 2026 loosening of SBA lending (7(a) plus 504 up to $10M) makes lenders care about key-person risk. The boomer owner cohort is aging.
revenue_model: $199 setup plus $19/month direct, wholesale at $99 per client to advisors, and API licensing to lenders.
non_obvious_insight: For the smallest businesses, succession usually means continuity, not sale. The distributor is the person who sells the life policy, who needs a reason to call every client each year.
first_30_days: Recruit five independent insurance agents or estate attorneys and offer white-label onboarding for 50 clients. Test whether successors can complete a simulated break-glass drill in under an hour.

title: Designer Proteins for Clear Protein Water
one_liner: AI-designed acid-stable proteins that stay clear at pH 2.8-3.5, replacing whey in clear protein drinks.
customer: RTD beverage and sports-nutrition brands making clear protein waters.
problem: Whey uniquely gives clear drinks at pH 2.8-3.5, and no alternative matches it, so brands cannot swap out scarce whey.
solution: Computationally design candidate proteins for acid solubility and clarity, express them through a contract fermentation partner, and deliver a first clear-drink ingredient.
why_now: Protein-design models and cheap gene synthesis matured in 2025-26, and Verley's FDA-cleared fermentation whey shows the regulatory path for fermentation-derived proteins.
revenue_model: Development fees of $50-150k per brand, then per-kg supply or licensing.
non_obvious_insight: Alt-protein failed by trying to replicate all of dairy. The real gap is a single functionality in a single premium beverage format.
first_30_days: Design about 20 candidates, test solubility and turbidity at pH 3 with cell-free expression, and pitch 10 clear-protein brands for paid development.

title: Operating System For Staff Cooperatives
one_liner: Digitise the exercise-book ledgers of workplace cooperatives, which are the cheapest credit pipe for Nigerian civil servants and teachers, then connect their idle surpluses to each other.
customer: Thrift-and-credit cooperative societies for teachers, nurses, civil servants, police, university staff and market associations. Their executive committees pay for the software. Later, the MFB or bank partner that funds wholesale lending between cooperatives.
problem: Outsiders assume Nigerian salary earners borrow from loan apps or MFBs. In reality a huge share borrow from staff cooperatives at about 10% flat per year, with payroll check-off giving near-zero defaults. But most societies run on Excel, exercise books and a treasurer's WhatsApp. Collapses come from embezzlement, unreconciled employer remittances, and members who cannot see their balances. Some cooperatives sit on idle surplus at 3-8% in a savings account while others in the same city ration loans to a waiting list.
solution: A WhatsApp-first ledger and treasury app: member savings and shares, loan applications with digital guarantors, approval workflows, automated reconciliation of employer check-off remittances against the deduction schedule, monthly member statements, and AGM voting and dividends. AI vision digitises the old exercise books on day one from phone photos. Once ledgers are clean and trusted, add an inter-cooperative wholesale line, routed through a bank or MFB partner, where surplus societies lend to constrained ones at a spread.
why_now: Multimodal AI can now read handwritten ledgers cheaply and reliably, which removes the onboarding barrier that killed earlier software. Tighter FCCPC rules on digital lenders have thinned out predatory apps and pushed members back toward cooperatives. Inflation and salary delays have raised demand for member loans. Open banking and cheaper payout APIs let cooperatives collect and disburse without paper cheques.
revenue_model: SaaS of about N25k-100k per month per cooperative, or N100-200 per member per month. A 0.5-1% spread on inter-cooperative wholesale loans. Fees on embedded products for members (insurance, school-fee financing, phones and gadgets) via the platform.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is not capital or customers but trusted records. Once a cooperative's ledger is clean and independent, it becomes a credit-bearing entity and its members can become a distribution channel, which is why the software is a wedge into wholesale lending. The check-off arrangement with the employer is the underwriting moat that no fintech can replicate.
first_30_days: Approach 10 cooperatives through teachers' unions, hospital staff associations and state civil-service networks. Digitise their books free using photo OCR, then start charging from month two. Get an accountant or cooperative-federation officer as a paid advisor for credibility. Track the first reconciliation win, such as finding a missing month of employer remittance, and use it as the case study.

title: Shared Effluent Utility for Depot Industrial Parks
angle: Pairing 2: Manufacturing reshoring/tariffs x Water infrastructure
one_liner: A common effluent treatment plant, sold by the gallon, for reshoring tenants at converted military depots and industrial parks.
customer: Redevelopment authorities and economic-development agencies for depots (Anniston, Pine Bluff, Red River, Tooele) and their tenants (magnet and mineral processors, plating shops, battery recyclers). Initial feasibility studies sell for $60-150k.
problem: Critical-mineral processors are taking leases at military depots, and processing generates hard wastewater streams. Permits, not machines, are the bottleneck that drove metal-heavy industry offshore. Each tenant building its own treatment is slow, expensive and a permit risk.
solution: Design, permit and later own and operate a shared pretreatment and zero-liquid-discharge utility with tenant tolling contracts. Begin with a permit-ready 'effluent envelope' study that gives site developers a defensible discharge limit and cost per gallon.
why_now: Federal money of about $2.9B committed to rare earths in June 2026, plus depot leases, plus permit fights over data centers (Cheyenne, Ohio) show water quality as a siting risk. Gradiant's $300M of fab wins prove appetite for industrial reuse.
revenue_model: Study fees, then long-term tolling contracts per gallon treated and a capital recovery charge. Optional public-private financing.
non_obvious_insight: India solved clustered industrial wastewater with common effluent plants decades ago. US reshoring will hit the same wall, and no US firm sells the shared plant as a utility.
first_30_days: Contact the redevelopment authorities at four depots with a $25k 'effluent envelope' scoping offer. Team a process engineer with a permitting lawyer. Line up two tenants' letters of interest to make the first study bankable.

title: Extranet Takeover Defense for Independent Hotels
one_liner: Managed monitoring and fraud response for hotels' OTA extranet logins and guest-messaging channels, the credential theft that turns into guest payment scams.
customer: Independent hotels, B&Bs and small STR managers of 10-150 rooms, their channel-manager and PMS resellers, and cyber insurers.
problem: Attackers phish or infect front-desk staff, take over OTA extranet accounts and message arriving guests from the genuine booking thread asking for payment via fraudulent links. The hotel absorbs chargebacks and reputational damage and can lose OTA account standing. These hotels have no IT staff and are too small for security vendors.
solution: A light service that watches for leaked credentials tied to the hotel's domain and staff emails, alerts on suspicious extranet login emails, flags guest messages containing external links or payment requests, and runs 10-minute staff phishing training. It adds a 24/7 hotline for incident response and a guest-facing 'how we ask for payment' page.
why_now: AI-written phishing in dozens of languages, widely reported hospitality-targeted credential theft campaigns in 2025, and merchant-model payments that concentrate risk in OTA accounts. Insurers are hardening cyber requirements.
revenue_model: EUR 49-149 per property per month, insurer commissions and per-incident response fees.
non_obvious_insight: The weak node is the hotel's front-desk laptop, not the OTA platform. The unit of attack is a booking thread the guest already trusts, so simple detection at the message level gives most of the protection.
first_30_days: Run a free credential-exposure scan for 100 hotel domains using public breach data. Send each hotel its results, convert 10 to paid, and partner with two hotel associations for distribution.

title: Fuel Surcharge Autopilot for Route-Based Services
one_liner: An add-on for field-service software that adds a transparent, index-linked, capped and self-expiring fuel line to invoices, and explains it to customers.
customer: Small route-based service businesses with 3-50 trucks: lawn and landscape, pest control, pool service, septic and portable toilets, HVAC and plumbing, mobile detailing and small waste haulers. They pay a monthly fee.
problem: Diesel is $6.53/gal, up $2.78 from a year ago, and gasoline is $4.48. Large firms absorb it. Cintas says 'we do not pass through any fuel surcharges', and Darden says sustained $6+ diesel would add 10-15 bps of cost. Small operators eat the increase or raise base prices and lose customers, because a surcharge added ad hoc looks like a scam.
solution: A plug-in for Jobber, Housecall Pro, Service Autopilot, Workiz and QuickBooks. The owner sets a base fuel price and a mileage-per-job model, and the plug-in computes a per-visit surcharge from the weekly EIA regional diesel or gasoline index. It adds a labelled invoice line with a cap, sends a one-time customer notice using tested wording, auto-reduces the charge when prices fall, and shows the owner recovered margin. The customer sees a public methodology page.
why_now: The Iran-conflict fuel shock has been running since spring, with diesel up 74% year over year, and it now appears in every large company's guidance (Darden, KB Home, General Mills, AutoZone, Stitch Fix). Small service businesses have had months of margin erosion and lack the pricing staff that large companies use.
revenue_model: $19-$49/month per business, or a 3-5% share of surcharge dollars collected. Add an annual 'fuel and route cost' benchmark report for FSM platforms as a lead generator.
non_obvious_insight: Fuel is a trust problem, not a math problem. The EIA shows diesel at $6.529/gal on Sept 21, 2026, up $2.780 year over year, with gasoline at $4.478 (https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/gasdiesel/). Cintas's CEO says 'it's a volatile situation with the price at the pump. We do not pass through any fuel surcharges' (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/09/24/cintas-ctas-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/). Darden's CFO puts the risk from sustained elevated diesel at 10-15 bps of sales and says its delivery fees sit in fixed-price contracts (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/09/24/darden-dri-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/). H.B. Fuller says small and mid-sized customers' order patterns swing on oil headlines (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/09/24/fuller-ful-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). Small operators cannot afford the customer backlash that large companies can, so a public formula, a cap and an automatic expiry are the product. Field-service platforms have not built this. The risk is that Jobber or ServiceTitan ship it natively, so the plan is to sell to the operator through a marketplace listing first and move quickly.
first_30_days: Build a minimal version as a Jobber integration or a Zapier plus Google Sheets tool driven by the EIA diesel API. Post in landscaping, pest and pool operator communities (Facebook groups, r/lawncare, LawnSite, PCT forums) offering a free tool and template customer letter. Get 20 operators to run it for one billing cycle, measure surcharge acceptance and cancellations, then start charging $29/month. Apply to the Jobber and Housecall Pro app marketplaces in parallel.

title: Court-Accounting Software for Family Conservators and Executors
one_liner: Statement-to-court-form automation for family members who must file annual accountings for a parent under conservatorship or through probate.
customer: Lay conservators, guardians and executors (Gen X children), plus probate attorneys, CPAs and professional fiduciaries who handle 20-200 cases.
problem: Roughly a million-plus adults are under guardianship or conservatorship, and probate cases rose about 32% from 2020 to 2024. Appointed family members must file county- and state-specific accountings with receipts and categories. Errors mean surcharges or removal, and lawyers or accountants charge $500-2,500 a filing.
solution: Connect bank accounts or upload statements, categorize against the state's court forms, flag court-sensitive items (gifts, related-party payments, unusual withdrawals), produce the accounting and receipt binder, and calendar deadlines. Include optional attorney review. Launch in California and Texas, where forms and rules are standardized.
why_now: 80+ growth means more incapacity and more estates. Elder fraud losses ($7.7B in 2025) are pushing courts to scrutinize guardians, and LLMs now parse statements accurately enough for categorization.
revenue_model: $399 a year per case for lay fiduciaries, and $79-150 per case per month for professional fiduciaries and law firms.
non_obvious_insight: Legal tech serves lawyers and estate-planning creation; nobody serves the family member who is legally required to be an amateur accountant. Court deadlines make the pain acute and the willingness to pay high.
first_30_days: Start with California and Texas. Build SEO around 'conservatorship accounting help', partner with probate attorneys, and sell the first 20 cases at $399.

title: Insurer-Funded Chronic Care for Diabetic Pets
angle: Finance (insurance economics, outcome-based payment) x Pets & animal health (vet-tech shortage, CGMs)
one_liner: A tech-led diabetes and kidney-disease program for insured pets, paid per member per month by insurers who capture the avoided ER claims.
customer: Mid-size pet insurers and MGAs (for example Fetch, Pumpkin, Odie and Lassie-type carriers) that need to cut claim severity. Independent clinics are the referral partner, and self-pay owners are the fallback.
problem: Diabetes and kidney disease in cats and dogs generate $3-6K a year in claims and emergency DKA admissions. AAHA's 2026 guidelines emphasize CGMs and once-daily insulins, but the workflow of monitoring, titration, coaching and refills has no owner. Vets are overloaded, vet techs are 2 per vet against a 4:1 ideal, and insurers' premiums are up 19.7% against animals up 9%, so they need to reduce claim costs rather than only raise prices.
solution: Sell insurers a PMPM disease-management pod: CGM starter kit, weekly data review by licensed vet techs under a supervising vet via the owner's clinic, protocol-driven insulin titration messages, refill logistics, and early-warning routing to the clinic before DKA. Enrollment is found in the insurer's claims file. Clinics are paid a titration-visit fee so they are not disintermediated. Insurers pay $40-70 PMPM with shared savings on avoided ER events.
why_now: AAHA split canine and feline diabetes guidelines in 2026 and put CGMs at the center. CGMs and long-acting insulins are arriving at once. Ambient AI and the vet-tech underuse make labor arbitrage possible. Insurers face repricing backlash, and remote VCPR rules are loosening piecemeal.
revenue_model: PMPM from insurers, gain-share on avoided claims, and CGM sensor and supply margin. Owner self-pay at $59 a month as a fallback.
non_obvious_insight: Insurers sit on the only longitudinal dataset and carry the financial downside. Clinics hold the license but not the time. This is Livongo-style economics: the payer who owns the downside pays for prevention, and vet techs are the labor arbitrage. Chronic care is a claims-cost product, not a telehealth product.
first_30_days: Convince one small MGA to share a de-identified diabetic-claims cohort and pilot a 200-pet program at cost. Recruit two RVTs and a supervising vet. If insurers are slow, launch a $59 a month owner-pay version through 5 clinics to get outcome data within 90-120 days.

title: Owner-Statement Auditor for Landlords With Property Managers
one_liner: Forward your property manager's monthly owner statements and get back the line items that don't add up: repairs with no invoice, charges on the wrong property, reserve draws that hide shortfalls, and true days vacant.
customer: Self-directed small investors with 2 to 30 doors who pay a third-party property manager, especially out-of-state owners. A second tier is the bookkeepers and CPAs who serve them and would white-label it.
problem: Every PM uses a different statement format, a different definition of 'net to owner' and a different fee schedule. Owners cannot tell whether a $400 repair really cost $900. Fees are often a percentage of the project, so the PM benefits from a bigger job. Thorough reconciliation takes 5 to 10 minutes per property per month, so most owners only glance at the deposit. Owners with several PMs end up rebuilding everything in QuickBooks or Excel by hand.
solution: An email-in service with no new PM software. The owner forwards PDF or CSV statements, or connects the PM portal export. Document extraction normalizes each statement into one chart of accounts. The owner also uploads the PM agreement, and the service extracts its fee terms and approval thresholds. Rules then flag: charges with no invoice; repeated repairs just under the approval threshold; the same vendor billed across properties for work meant for one; reserve movements that mask a shortfall; late-fee handling that differs from the contract; and fees booked in the wrong month. It also computes true days vacant (turn time included) as opposed to the 'days on market' PMs report, plus maintenance cost per door and the share of work orders closed on the first visit. Output is a one-page monthly report and a ready-to-send dispute email. An optional human bookkeeper review is the upsell.
why_now: Sept 2026 BiggerPockets threads show owners asking these exact questions with no tool that answers them. Landlord banking tools (Baselane, RentRedi) still 'aren't really bookkeeping', as one thread puts it. Extracting structured data from messy PM statement PDFs became cheap and reliable with current document-AI models. That turns a manual forensic accounting service into a $9-per-door product.
revenue_model: $9 per door per month, or $99 per property per year. A one-time $199 backfill audit of the trailing 12 months acts as the lead magnet and first revenue. A bookkeeper and CPA white-label plan at about $49 per client per month. The audit could later be paired with recovery: for any overcharge that gets refunded, take 15%.
non_obvious_insight: Owners are not asking for another PM platform. They want a neutral second set of eyes, and PMs will never build one because they are the party being checked. Evidence: 'How do you verify your PM net deposit matches the statement each month?' (19 replies) lists wrong-property charges, repairs with no invoice, and reserve adjustments that absorb shortfalls, at 5-10 minutes per property (https://www.biggerpockets.com/forums/899/topics/1293899-how-do-you-verify-your-pm-net-deposit-matches-the-statement-each-month). 'Every PM seems to send a different statement format, a different definition of net to owner' (https://www.biggerpockets.com/forums/963/topics/1292833-owners-with-multiple-pms-how-do-you-keep-one-clean-view-across-statements). Owners can't verify whether a $400 repair needed $900, and 'days on market is not days vacant' (https://www.biggerpockets.com/forums/963/topics/1301673-what-actually-keeps-out-of-state-landlords-up-at-night). A repair-transparency survey quote reads: 'I couldn't tell which line items were fair and which were padded' (https://www.biggerpockets.com/forums/52/topics/1302340-small-landlords-with-a-pm-2-minute-survey-on-fees-and-repair-estimates).
first_30_days: Week 1: reply in the threads above and offer a free 12-month statement audit to 10 owners in exchange for anonymized statements. Build the audit by hand with a spreadsheet, an extraction prompt and a rules checklist. Weeks 2 to 3: deliver the audits, and use the discrepancies found as case studies. Week 4: convert to the $199 backfill and $9-per-door subscription, and pitch three real-estate bookkeepers on the white-label plan. Target: 10 paying owners and 2 bookkeeper partners.

title: Genetic-Resource Provenance Ledger for Bio-AI
one_liner: Track which genetic resources and sequences, physical and digital, feed a company's models and pipelines, so it can prove Nagoya compliance today and estimate Cali Fund exposure tomorrow.
customer: Nature-sourced discovery and AI-model builders, starting with the ABS, sustainability and legal units of large pharma, enzyme, ag, food and cosmetics groups, plus sample-collecting AI biotechs such as those mining plants and microbes.
problem: Trend chain: sequence-trained foundation models (Evo 2 trained on 9.3 trillion nucleotides across the tree of life) and proprietary sampling programs (Basecamp's Trillion Gene Atlas, Enveda's sourcing) make genetic-resource provenance a first-class asset. The Cali Fund (launched Feb 2025) asks large DSI users for roughly 1% of profits or 0.1% of revenue, but had only two contributions totaling $6,000 by August 2026. COP17 (Yerevan, Oct 19-30, 2026) is due to confirm rates and allocation. Nagoya duties for physical samples already exist, and public sequence metadata on origin is sparse. Nobody instruments any of it.
solution: Software plus advisory. Ingest sample logs and training or data manifests. Map accessions to origin metadata, flag ABS status, model Cali Fund exposure scenarios, and generate audit-ready disclosures and a 'DSI provenance statement' for model cards. Broker PIC/MAT permit packages for new sampling. Phase 1 revenue comes from existing Nagoya duties on physical collections.
why_now: COP17 is weeks away, and national DSI rules may move faster than the fund. The fund's weak uptake means the near-term product must be Nagoya and provenance assurance, with DSI as an option that COP17 could harden.
revenue_model: $25-120k annual license or advisory for enterprises, $5-15k per collection-permit package, and one-off audit sprints.
non_obvious_insight: The DSI debate is framed as a tax question, but the scarce asset is the sequence-to-origin map. If COP17 or national laws harden, whoever holds the provenance graph sells compliance to everyone. If they do not, the same graph sells 'clean provenance' assurance to acquirers and pharma partners.
first_30_days: Build a lead magnet: a 'DSI exposure snapshot' of a public training corpus or a company's sequence set. Offer 10 free snapshots to sustainability and legal leads. Recruit 2 sample-collecting AI biotechs with live ABS contracts as design partners. Partner with an ABS law firm.

title: GLP-1 Size-Curve Index for Apparel Planners
one_liner: A monthly 'size-shift index' that tells merchandise planners, airlines and furniture makers how GLP-1 adoption is moving their customers' bodies.
customer: Merchandise planners and size-curve analysts at apparel, footwear and outdoor brands and off-price retailers, plus airline, cruise, furniture and medical-equipment planners.
problem: Households with a GLP-1 user doubled to ~22%, and users lose double-digit percentages of body weight in a year. Retailers still plan size curves on last year's sell-through, which lags, causing markdowns on the wrong sizes. CFOs are already modeling downstream effects (Jefferies estimates ~$600M/yr airline fuel savings).
solution: Build an index by region, age and gender from licensed or partner data (pharmacy-fill proxies where affordable, retailer size and returns data, sizing surveys, public health data) and forecast size-curve migration by category. Deliver an API, a quarterly briefing, and a custom-model add-on.
why_now: Adoption accelerated after the 2026 pill launches. BCG and GoodRx data show measurable spend shifts (less pasta and bakery, more fragrance, skincare and supplements), so consumer-goods planners are hunting for leading indicators.
revenue_model: $40-120k/year per retailer or brand, plus $20-60k custom-modeling projects.
non_obvious_insight: Sell-through is a lagging indicator, and the drug adoption curve by ZIP is a leading one. It is a healthcare-adjacent data business with no clinical regulation if built on aggregated data, so a two-person team can sell it to non-healthcare budgets.
first_30_days: Build v0 from public data (NHANES, BRFSS, Google Trends) plus a 2,000-person sizing survey. Email 30 planners with a free size-shift report for one category and offer partner-data-in-exchange pricing. Sign one $15k pilot.
